parts.title: Word List 1
parts.content:
Word List 1

Detailed Meanings

😎
rewrite [ri:ˈraɪt] v.
to write again, especially in a different way. (viết lại)
"The author had to rewrite the ending of the book." (Tác giả đã phải viết lại phần kết của cuốn sách.)
😎
decade [ˈdek.eɪd] n.
a period of ten years. (thập niên, mười năm)
"He has been working here for a decade." (Anh ấy đã làm việc ở đây được một thập niên.)
😎
archaeologist [ˌɑːr.kiˈɑː.lə.dʒɪst] n.
a person who studies human history and prehistory through the excavation of sites and the analysis of artifacts. (nhà khảo cổ học)
"The archaeologist discovered ancient ruins." (Nhà khảo cổ học đã phát hiện ra những tàn tích cổ đại.)
😎
deny [dɪˈnaɪ] v.
to state that one refuses to admit the truth or existence of. (chối bỏ, phủ nhận)
"He denied any involvement in the crime." (Anh ta phủ nhận mọi sự liên quan đến vụ phạm tội.)
😎
originate [əˈrɪdʒ.ə.neɪt] v.
to have a specified beginning. (bắt nguồn từ)
"The disease originated in Africa." (Căn bệnh này bắt nguồn từ Châu Phi.)
😎
disprove [dɪsˈpruːv] v.
to prove that something is false. (bác bỏ)
"The new evidence disproves his theory." (Bằng chứng mới bác bỏ lý thuyết của anh ta.)
😎
fossil [ˈfɑː.səl] n.
the remains or impression of a prehistoric organism preserved in petrified form. (hóa thạch)
"They found a dinosaur fossil." (Họ tìm thấy hóa thạch khủng long.)
😎
skeleton [ˈskel.ə.t̬ən] n.
an internal or external framework of bone. (bộ xương)
"The human skeleton consists of 206 bones." (Bộ xương người bao gồm 206 chiếc xương.)
😎
though [ðoʊ] adv.
however; nevertheless. (mặc dù, tuy nhiên)
"He is old, though still active." (Anh ấy đã già, tuy nhiên vẫn rất năng động.)
😎
species [ˈspiː.ʃiːz] n.
a group of living organisms consisting of similar individuals. (chủng loài)
"There are many species of birds here." (Có rất nhiều loài chim ở đây.)
😎
Homo sapiens [ˌhoʊ.moʊ ˈseɪ.pi.enz] n.
the primate species to which modern humans belong. (người hiện đại)
"Homo sapiens evolved in Africa." (Người hiện đại tiến hóa ở Châu Phi.)
😎
genetic [dʒəˈnet̬.ɪk] adj.
relating to genes or heredity. (thuộc về gen)
"They conducted genetic testing." (Họ đã tiến hành xét nghiệm di truyền.)
😎
genesis [ˈdʒen.ə.sɪs] n.
the origin or mode of formation of something. (căn nguyên, nguồn gốc)
"The genesis of the project was simple." (Nguồn gốc của dự án rất đơn giản.)
😎
Eurocentrics [ˌjʊr.oʊˈsen.trɪks] n.
people who believe that European culture is preeminent. (người cho rằng con người bắt nguồn từ châu Âu)
"Eurocentrics believed culture started in Europe." (Những người theo thuyết dĩ Âu vi trung tin rằng văn hóa bắt nguồn từ châu Âu.)
😎
cave painting [keɪv ˈpeɪn.t̬ɪŋ] n.
a prehistoric picture on the interior of a cave. (tranh vẽ trong hang động)
"The cave painting depicted wild animals." (Bức tranh hang động mô tả các loài động vật hoang dã.)
😎
comfort [ˈkʌm.fɚt] v.
to soothe in time of affliction or distress. (an ủi)
"She comforted her crying child." (Cô ấy an ủi đứa con đang khóc của mình.)
😎
symbol [ˈsɪm.bəl] n.
a mark or character used as a conventional representation of an object. (ký hiệu, biểu tượng)
"The dove is a symbol of peace." (Chim bồ câu là biểu tượng của hòa bình.)
😎
cultural [ˈkʌl.tʃɚ.əl] adj.
relating to the ideas, customs, and social behavior of a society. (thuộc văn hóa)
"The city has a rich cultural heritage." (Thành phố có một di sản văn hóa phong phú.)
😎
pretension [prɪˈten.ʃən] n.
a claim or the assertion of a claim to something. (ý muốn, kỳ vọng)
"He has no pretension to being an expert." (Anh ta không có kỳ vọng trở thành chuyên gia.)
😎
beg [beɡ] v.
to ask someone earnestly or humbly for something. (xin phép, cầu xin)
"I beg to differ with your opinion." (Xin phép cho tôi có ý kiến khác với bạn.)
😎
I beg to differ [aɪ beɡ tə ˈdɪf.ɚ] phrase
a polite way of disagreeing. (Xin phép cho tôi có ý kiến khác.)
"I beg to differ; I think you are wrong." (Xin phép cho tôi có ý kiến khác; tôi nghĩ bạn đã sai.)
😎
challenge [ˈtʃæl.ɪndʒ] v.
to dispute the truth or validity of. (thách thức, phản đối)
"They challenged the results of the election." (Họ phản đối kết quả cuộc bầu cử.)
😎
artistic [ɑːrˈtɪs.tɪk] adj.
having or revealing natural creative skill. (thuộc nghệ thuật)
"My sister is very artistic and paints beautifully." (Em gái tôi rất có khiếu nghệ thuật và vẽ rất đẹp.)
😎
migrate [ˈmaɪ.ɡreɪt] v.
to move from one region or habitat to another. (di cư)
"Birds migrate south for the winter." (Các loài chim di cư về phía nam vào mùa đông.)
😎
dig up [dɪɡ ʌp] phrasal v.
to discover or reveal something that has been hidden. (đào lên, xới lên)
"They dug up some ancient coins." (Họ đã đào lên một vài đồng tiền cổ đại.)

sections.title: Exercise 1: Choose the correct word to fill in the blank.

questions.content: The ________ discovered ancient ruins in the desert.
questions.explanation: An archaeologist is a person who studies human history and prehistory through the excavation of sites.

questions.explanation: A fossil is the remains or impression of a prehistoric organism preserved in petrified form.

questions.explanation: Migrate means to move from one region or habitat to another.

questions.content: The disease is believed to ________ in Africa.
questions.explanation: Originate means to have a specified beginning.

questions.explanation: Dig up means to discover or reveal something that has been hidden.

sections.title: Exercise 2: Choose the word that best matches the definition.

questions.content: A period of ten years.
questions.explanation: A decade is a period of ten years.

questions.content: An internal or external framework of bone.
questions.explanation: A skeleton is an internal or external framework of bone.

questions.content: To prove that something is false.
questions.explanation: Disprove means to prove that something is false.

sections.title: Exercise 3: Mark each statement True or False.

questions.content: "Homo sapiens" refers to the primate species to which modern humans belong.
questions.explanation: True. Homo sapiens is the primate species to which modern humans belong.

questions.content: "Cave painting" refers to a modern picture on the exterior of a building.
questions.explanation: False. A cave painting is a prehistoric picture on the interior of a cave.

questions.content: To "comfort" someone means to make them feel worse.
questions.explanation: False. To comfort means to soothe in time of affliction or distress.

parts.title: Word List 2
parts.content:
Word List 2

Detailed Meanings

😎
evidence [ˈev.ə.dəns] n.
the available body of facts or information indicating whether a belief or proposition is true. (chứng cứ)
"The police found evidence at the crime scene." (Cảnh sát tìm thấy chứng cứ tại hiện trường vụ án.)
😎
claim [kleɪm] v.
to state or assert that something is the case. (tuyên bố, cho là)
"He claims to be an expert." (Anh ấy tuyên bố mình là một chuyên gia.)
😎
evolve [ɪˈvɑːlv] v.
to develop gradually, especially from a simple to a more complex form. (tiến hóa)
"The company has evolved into a major corporation." (Công ty đã phát triển thành một tập đoàn lớn.)
😎
scrape [skreɪp] v.
to drag or pull a hard or sharp implement across (a surface). (nạo, vét)
"She scraped the mud off her shoes." (Cô ấy cạo bùn khỏi giày.)
😎
impressive [ɪmˈpres.ɪv] adj.
evoking admiration through size, quality, or skill. (ấn tượng)
"His resume is quite impressive." (Bản lý lịch của anh ấy khá ấn tượng.)
😎
collection [kəˈlek.ʃən] n.
the action or process of collecting someone or something. (bộ sưu tập)
"He has a large stamp collection." (Anh ấy có một bộ sưu tập tem lớn.)
😎
artefact [ˈɑːr.t̬ə.fækt] n.
an object made by a human being, typically an item of cultural or historical interest. (đồ tạo tác)
"They found Roman artefacts in the field." (Họ tìm thấy những đồ tạo tác La Mã ở cánh đồng.)
😎
ochre [ˈoʊ.kɚ] n.
an earthy pigment containing ferric oxide, typically with clay, varying from light yellow to brown or red. (đất son, hoàng thổ)
"They used ochre to paint their bodies." (Họ sử dụng đất son để sơn lên cơ thể.)
😎
mineral [ˈmɪn.ɚ.əl] n.
a solid inorganic substance of natural occurrence. (khoáng chất)
"Diamonds are a valuable mineral." (Kim cương là một khoáng chất có giá trị.)
😎
crush [krʌʃ] v.
to deform, pulverize, or force inwards by compressing forcefully. (nghiền ra)
"They crushed the rocks to make gravel." (Họ nghiền đá để làm sỏi.)
😎
decoration [ˌdek.əˈreɪ.ʃən] n.
the process or art of decorating or adorning something. (sự trang hoàng)
"We bought some Christmas decorations." (Chúng tôi đã mua một số đồ trang trí Giáng sinh.)
😎
pattern [ˈpæt̬.ɚn] n.
a repeated decorative design. (mẫu, kiểu)
"The fabric has a beautiful pattern." (Vải có một hoa văn đẹp.)
😎
engrave [ɪnˈɡreɪv] v.
to cut or carve a text or design on the surface of a hard object. (khắc, chạm)
"He engraved his name on the ring." (Anh ấy đã khắc tên mình lên chiếc nhẫn.)
😎
intentional [ɪnˈten.ʃən.əl] adj.
done on purpose; deliberate. (cố ý, có dụng ý)
"The damage was not intentional." (Thiệt hại không phải là cố ý.)
😎
geometric [ˌdʒiː.əˈmet.rɪk] adj.
relating to geometry, or according to its methods. (thuộc hình học)
"The building has geometric shapes." (Tòa nhà có các hình khối hình học.)
😎
motif [moʊˈtiːf] n.
a decorative design or pattern. (họa tiết, hoa văn trang trí)
"The wallpaper features a floral motif." (Giấy dán tường có hoa văn hoa lá.)
😎
date [deɪt] v.
to establish or ascertain the date of. (xác định ngày tháng, xác định niên đại)
"Scientists dated the fossils to 70,000 years ago." (Các nhà khoa học xác định niên đại của hóa thạch là 70.000 năm trước.)
😎
excavate [ˈek.skə.veɪt] v.
to make a hole or channel by digging. (khai quật, đào)
"They plan to excavate the ancient site." (Họ dự định khai quật địa điểm cổ đại.)
😎
turn up [tɝːn ʌp] phrasal v.
to be found, especially by chance. (bới lên, phơi trần)
"The missing ring turned up under the sofa." (Chiếc nhẫn bị mất đã được tìm thấy dưới ghế sofa.)
😎
given [ˈɡɪv.ən] prep.
taking into account. (căn cứ vào)
"Given the circumstances, he did well." (Căn cứ vào hoàn cảnh, anh ấy đã làm tốt.)
😎
strata [ˈstræt̬.ə] n.
a layer or a series of layers of rock in the ground. (địa tầng, vỉa, giai cấp)
"They found fossils in the lower strata." (Họ tìm thấy hóa thạch ở các địa tầng bên dưới.)
😎
add to [æd tuː] phrasal v.
to increase the size, number, or amount of something. (bổ sung vào)
"The new evidence adds to their theory." (Bằng chứng mới bổ sung thêm cho lý thuyết của họ.)
😎
confidence [ˈkɑːn.fə.dəns] n.
the feeling or belief that one can rely on someone or something. (sự tin tưởng)
"She has great confidence in her abilities." (Cô ấy có sự tin tưởng lớn vào khả năng của mình.)
😎
prick [prɪk] v.
to cause someone to feel a sudden small pain. (làm tan vỡ, cắn rứt)
"Europe's pretensions may be pricked again." (Kỳ vọng của châu Âu có thể bị làm tan vỡ lần nữa.)
😎
turn out [tɝːn aʊt] phrasal v.
to prove to be the case. (hóa ra, thành ra)
"The stranger turned out to be her brother." (Người lạ mặt hóa ra lại là anh trai cô ấy.)

sections.title: Exercise 3: Mark each statement True or False.

questions.content: "Ochre" is an earthy pigment containing ferric oxide.
questions.explanation: True. Ochre is an earthy pigment.

questions.content: A "motif" is an accidental pattern or design.
questions.explanation: False. A motif is a decorative design or pattern.

questions.content: "Confidence" means a feeling of doubt or uncertainty.
questions.explanation: False. Confidence is the feeling or belief that one can rely on someone or something.

parts.title: Comprehensive Reading
parts.content:
Comprehensive Reading

But Is It Art?

A cave in South Africa may rewrite human history

For the whole of the 19th and the first decades of the 20th centuries, archaeologists in the West denied that mankind had originated in Africa. The first humans, surely, must have been Europeans. That idea was disproved by Raymond Dart in the 1920s. He discovered fossil human bones in South Africa. These skeletons, though, were earlier species than Homo sapiens. Then, in the 1980s, genetic work by Allan Wilson showed that modern man, too, had an African genesis. But at least the Eurocentrics had cave paintings to comfort them. The oldest of these symbols of humanity's cultural pretensions were European. Therefore culture was invented in Europe. So there!

Chris Henshilwood, a South African archaeologist, begs to differ. He is challenging the theory that artistic culture first developed in Europe about 35,000 years ago, after people had migrated out of Africa. He has dug up evidence which, he claims, shows that such behaviour evolved over 70,000 years ago—and in Africa.

This evidence comes from a seaside cave called Blombos, two hours drive from Cape Town. Mr Henshilwood and his team have spent years scraping an impressive collection of artefacts out of this cave. In particular, Blombos was full of bits of ochre, a mineral that can be crushed and used to paint the skin for decoration, and for protection from the sun.

That is not unusual; many African caves contain bits of ochre. But two stones found in recent years have patterns engraved on them. This, according to Mr Henshilwood, means they are "intentional images and can be considered a complex geometric motif". Tests on the sand they were buried in, using two different dating techniques (thermoluminescence and oxygen-isotope analysis), suggest they are between 70,000 and 80,000 years old. If that is right, they constitute the world's oldest works of art. In February, Thabo Mbeki, South Africa's president, opened parliament with the stones at his side, and said he was delighted to have proof that Africa gave birth to modern man.

One African cave does not, of course, compare with the Neolithic cultural riches dug up across Western Europe. But there are, according to Mr Henshilwood, many more caves to explore and excavate near Blombos, so more art may turn up. Given that things can move between strata due to the activities of burrowing animals, a few more examples would certainly add to confidence that he is right about the date. On the other hand, according to Mr Henshilwood, "No one has challenged our methods yet." Europe's pretensions may be pricked again, as the first artists turn out to have been African.

questions.content: What did archaeologists in the West deny for a long time?
options: That early humans could make art.
questions.explanation: The text states: 'archaeologists in the West denied that mankind had originated in Africa.'

questions.content: Who discovered fossil human bones in South Africa in the 1920s?
questions.explanation: The passage says: 'That idea was disproved by Raymond Dart in the 1920s. He discovered fossil human bones in South Africa.'

questions.content: What is ochre?
options: A hard mineral used for tools.
A soft stone containing iron oxide.
questions.explanation: According to the text, 'Ochre is a soft stone containing iron oxide.'

questions.content: What kind of patterns were scraped on the pieces found at Blombos?
questions.explanation: The text describes: 'The patterns consist of diagonal lines and triangles.'

questions.content: Why are the discoveries at Blombos Cave important?
options: They prove humans originated in Europe.
They show early humans were purely hunters.
They suggest early humans had complex minds.
They represent a sudden creative explosion in Europe.
questions.explanation: The passage concludes: 'The discoveries are important because they suggest early humans had complex minds.'
